title: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 through October 20, 2027, and for other purposes.
official_title: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 through October 20, 2027, and for other purposes.
summary: Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act lets the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence jointly authorize the targeting of people reasonably believed to be outside the United States to collect foreign intelligence, for up to a year at a time, and states that the regular FISA court-order process is not required for that targeting. This bill replaces the shut-off trigger, which was set at two years after the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act was approved on April 20, 2024, with a fixed repeal date of October 20, 2027, and rewrites the matching rule for orders already in effect when that date arrives.
brief: Sets a fixed October 20, 2027 repeal date for FISA Title VII surveillance authorities in place of the trigger tied to the 2024 reform law, with no new limits attached.

top_lines.headline: What Title VII Authorizes
subs: Attorney General and DNI jointly authorize targeting of people located abroad
Each joint authorization runs up to 1 year
Regular FISA court-order process not required for that targeting
Providers can be directed in writing to supply information and assistance
FBI queries of the collected data using U.S. person terms need supervisor approval

top_lines.headline: What This Bill Changes
subs: Fixed October 20, 2027 repeal date replaces the two-year trigger
Old trigger ran two years from April 20, 2024
No new limits, oversight, or reporting attached

top_lines.headline: Orders Already In Effect
subs: Grandfather clause rewritten to cite Title VII as a whole
Orders and directives keep running until they expire

top_lines.headline: Effective Date
subs: Takes effect on the earlier of enactment or April 19, 2026

likelihoodReason: The sponsor is a Republican and the bill had no cosponsors. The rule providing for its consideration, H. Res. 1175, was rejected on the House floor 197-228 on April 17, 2026 (Roll no. 124), so the House never reached a vote on the bill itself, and the committees of referral have not reported it.

sections.label: Section 1 — Extension of Authorities of Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978

items.main: Rewrites the Title VII sunset in Section 403(b)(1) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 so that Title VII is repealed effective October 20, 2027.
items.detail: The bill strikes the words effective two years after and everything following them through the period, and inserts a clause repealing title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.) effective October 20, 2027. The trigger being replaced runs two years from the approval of the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act, Public Law 118-49, on April 20, 2024.

items.main: Applies the same fixed date to Section 403(b)(2), which governs a conforming amendment to the federal criminal wiretap statute.
items.detail: Section 403(b)(2) of Public Law 110-261 provides that, on the sunset date, 18 U.S.C. 2511(2)(a)(ii)(A) is amended by striking the words or a court order pursuant to section 704 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978. Subparagraph (A) is one of two showings that let a communications provider lawfully furnish surveillance assistance, the other being a written certification under subparagraph (B). The bill replaces the paragraph opener that set that amendment two years after enactment of the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act with one reading Effective October 20, 2027.

items.main: Rewrites the heading and cross-references of Section 404(b), the clause that keeps existing Title VII orders alive past the repeal date.
items.detail: Section 404(b)(1) of Public Law 110-261 provides that any order, authorization, or directive issued under title VII continues in effect until it expires, and paragraph (2) keeps title VII itself applying to those orders until the later of their expiration or final judgment in related litigation. The bill retitles paragraph (1) to refer to the repeal date instead of the two-year trigger, and in both paragraphs replaces the recital naming section 101(a), the FISA Amendments Reauthorization Act of 2017, and the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act with the plain citation 50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.

items.main: Sets all of the amendments to take effect on the earlier of the date of enactment or April 19, 2026.
items.detail: April 19, 2026 is the day before the two-year mark from the April 20, 2024 approval of the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act, so the amendments would attach before the existing sunset trigger arrived even if enactment came later.

underreported.summary: Replaces the description of Title VII inside the Section 404(b) grandfather clause. Where that clause now protects orders issued under title VII as amended by section 101(a), the FISA Amendments Reauthorization Act of 2017, and the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act, the bill would have it protect orders issued under title VII (50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.) without naming those amending acts.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill is captioned as extending Title VII authorities through October 20, 2027, and this subsection changes no date. It edits the heading and the internal citations of the clause that decides how long already-issued orders and directives survive the repeal.

gaps: The bill sets a fixed October 20, 2027 repeal date but attaches no condition, review, or reporting requirement to the eighteen months it adds beyond the April 20, 2026 trigger it replaces.

The bill is captioned as extending the Title VII authorities and for other purposes, but the text contains only the sunset-date changes, the conforming cross-reference changes, and the effective-date clause.

modified: Section 403(b)(1) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-261) — Title VII repeal trigger changed from two years after April 20, 2024 to a fixed October 20, 2027

Section 403(b)(2) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-261) — effective date of the conforming amendment to 18 U.S.C. 2511(2)(a)(ii)(A) changed from two years after enactment of the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act to October 20, 2027

Section 404(b)(1) and (2) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-261) — the recital naming section 101(a), the FISA Amendments Reauthorization Act of 2017 and the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act replaced with the citation 50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq., and the paragraph (1) heading changed to refer to the repeal date
